patch_description: GPU balancedness (0.66) is the dominant weakness. The existing `_refine_packing` only tries one swap per round (heaviest pack's smallest item ↔ lightest pack's largest item) and stops as soon as that single extreme pair fails, which gets stuck in poor local optima. I replace it with a stronger local search that, for the most-loaded pack's smallest item, evaluates the best partner pack among *all* other packs (each contributing its largest item) and picks the swap that minimizes the resulting maximum pack load. Cardinality and rank-slot constraints are preserved exactly (swapped items inherit each other's pack and rank slots), so all downstream map construction (`inverse`, `gather`) still works verbatim. To keep it fast, the inner search runs on plain Python lists per layer with early termination when no improving swap exists, and per-pack item lists are maintained incrementally so each round costs O(n) instead of O(P·n) tensor ops. Since `balanced_packing` is used both for node packing (Step 1) and GPU packing (Step 3), the improved swap heuristic directly raises GPU-level balance without touching the risky hierarchical plumbing. More refinement rounds (64) are affordable because the loop breaks as soon as convergence is reached.
